# A Working Knowledge of R for Researchers

R is not a general-purpose language, and that is its strength. It was built by
statisticians for data analysis, and almost every classical and modern method
you will need is one `install.packages()` away.

## Installing and Starting

Install R from CRAN, then install RStudio (or use VS Code). For this book,
install:

```r
install.packages(c(
  "tidyverse", "ggplot2", "dplyr", "readr",
  "boot", "car", "effsize", "pwr", "MASS",
  "broom", "knitr", "rmarkdown", "microbenchmark"
))
```

## The Vector Is the Atom

Almost everything in R is a vector. A "scalar" is just a vector of length one.

```r
latencies <- c(12.3, 11.9, 13.7, 12.1, 15.0)
mean(latencies)        # 13.0
sd(latencies)          # 1.27
length(latencies)      # 5
latencies[latencies > 12]
```

## Data Frames

A data frame is a table where columns can be different types.

```r
df <- data.frame(
  system  = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 5),
  latency = c(12.3, 11.9, 13.7, 12.1, 15.0,
              10.1, 10.5,  9.8, 11.2, 10.0)
)
aggregate(latency ~ system, data = df, FUN = mean)
```

## The Tidyverse Idiom

```r
library(dplyr)
df |>
  group_by(system) |>
  summarise(mean_lat = mean(latency),
            sd_lat   = sd(latency),
            n        = n())
```

## Reading Data

```r
library(readr)
runs <- read_csv("experiment_runs.csv")
```

## Reproducibility From Day One

Set a seed for any random procedure, record `sessionInfo()` in your artifacts,
and prefer scripts over interactive sessions.

```r
set.seed(20260525)
sessionInfo()
```
